qa.q: Rory, do you think you are a polite person?
qa.a: Well, I certainly try to be well-mannered, especially with people I don't know well in formal context. Uh, I think it's important for making a good person impression, isn't it?

qa.q: Do you think people should be polite?
qa.a: Well, most of the time, yes. People just want to get on, don't they? Um, and being polite helps with that. Um, it also helps smooth things over in fraught situations.

qa.q: How do people in your culture show good manners towards others?
qa.a: Well, they make eye contact, shake hands, uh, generally avoid swearing and foul language, and they dress for the occasion as well. And there are other things like respecting personal space, uh, conversational and social boundaries too.

qa.q: Who taught you to be polite?
qa.a: I think it was my parents and my maternal grandmother in the main. Uh, although teachers and friends and others, like sort of played supporting roles in that sense. I think in most cultures, it falls to the adults around you to take part in this aspect of socialization, uh, doesn't it?

qa.q: Is it important to be polite in your country?
qa.a: Well, people have this impression that British people are sort of very neurotic about good manners and being well-behaved, but actually, I would argue that we're pretty average in this regard. So, compared to countries like Korea or Japan where there are sort of rules that govern the behavior of everything. Um, and then if you talk about places like America, people air their views on everything with little regard for other people's feelings. So, we're sort of occupying the middle ground.

qa.q: How important is politeness for you?
qa.a: Well, I didn't realize it until the other day that it is actually quite a priority for me, especially when I deal with people I don't know. Like, I'm really put off when people don't have an opening in their emails and just go straight to whatever request they might have. Um, pleases and thank yous are also something that, like, helps me personally get invested in people and their problems. Um, I know it seems a bit like window dressing, but at least in my case, it serves a useful purpose.

qa.q: Do you generally think that people are more polite now?
qa.a: I don't know how you would measure that. I, I say this often, but I really don't know how to tell. Um, I think amongst my group of friends, when we are dealing with people that we don't know, we're quite polite. But we're not polite with each other. But then that's quite true of close friends everywhere, I think.

qa.q: Did Russian people seem rude to you?
qa.a: Did they? I would say that Russians are quite short when they speak with you. And even now, after I've been here for so many years, it still seems that way to me from time to time.
